author: Pallas, 1811
status: 나그네새·겨울철새, 해마다 수천 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
habitat: 강 하구, 갯벌, 개활지, 논, 초습지
summary: 해마다 수천 마리가 찾아오는 나그네새이자 겨울철새로, 강 하구, 갯벌, 개활지, 논, 초습지에서 지낸다. 겨울에는 어미새가 어린새와 가족 무리를 이루고, 이동 시기에는 여러 가족이 모여 큰 무리가 된다. 조개류와 곤충, 옥수수와 벼 낟알, 풀씨, 풀뿌리 등을 먹으며, 경계심이 아주 강해 사람이 다가오면 망을 보던 개체의 신호에 무리 전체가 목과 머리를 들고 날아오를 채비를 한다. 극동아시아에만 사는 종으로 몽골 동부와 러시아·중국 국경 지역에서 번식하고 중국 양쯔강 유역, 한국, 일본 이즈미에서 겨울을 나며, 국내에서는 철원에 가장 많고 한강 하구, 임진강 유역, 순천만, 구미 해평습지, 주남저수지, 낙동강 하구 등에서도 일부가 월동한다.

points.en: bare red skin around the eye
white tertials covering the folded wing

art.subject: White-naped Crane (Grus vipio), adult, as seen in Korean winter fields and estuaries from November to March: crown, nape and a broad stripe down the back of the neck white; a patch of bare red skin around the eye, reaching forward to the bill base and edged with fine black bristles; throat white; foreneck and sides of the neck dark slate-grey, the grey narrowing to a point on the side of the head. Body dark slate-grey; upperwing coverts paler silvery-grey; tertials long, pale whitish-grey, drooping over the tail like a bustle. Primaries and secondaries black. Bill pale greenish-yellow; legs and feet pinkish-red.
art.pose: standing alert with head raised in a harvested rice field
art.scene: Korean winter harvested rice paddies near a river estuary and mudflats; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view standing: red facial skin around the eye, white crown and hindneck stripe, dark grey foreneck and neck sides, slate-grey body, pale whitish tertials drooping over the folded wing, pinkish-red legs
adult, in flight seen from above: neck stretched forward and legs trailing, slate-grey body, pale silvery-grey upperwing coverts contrasting with black primaries and secondaries
juvenile (first winter), side view standing: head and upper neck tawny yellowish-brown from crown to hindneck, no red facial skin yet, grey body mottled brownish
art.build: Large crane, about 127cm, much taller than a Grey Heron and slightly smaller than a Red-crowned Crane. Long neck, small head; bill straight, about as long as the head or a little longer. Legs very long, pinkish-red, with bare tibia. At rest the folded wings are covered by the long, pale, drooping tertials that hide the short tail. In flight the neck is stretched forward and the legs trail well beyond the tail; the upperwing shows pale silvery-grey coverts contrasting with black flight feathers. In winter moves in family groups of two adults and one or two young.
avoid: Do not paint a black neck or a white body — that is Red-crowned Crane.
Do not paint black or dark legs; this species has pinkish-red legs.
Do not paint a black throat with a white stripe behind the eye (Common Crane) or an all-white head and upper neck (Hooded Crane).
Do not put the red only on the crown; the red bare skin surrounds the eye.
